title: Step 1: Hook - The Blindfold Taste Test
content: Imagine you are blindfolded and holding your nose. Can you tell the difference between a piece of apple and a piece of potato just by chewing? Surprisingly, they might taste exactly the same! Let's uncover the secret connection between tasting, smelling, and eating.

title: Step 2: Socratic Thinking - The Magic Bumps
content: If you look closely at your tongue in a mirror, you'll see hundreds of tiny bumps. What do you think those bumps do? And why does a piece of plain roti or bread taste sweeter the longer you chew it?

content.title: Step 3: Discovery - The Flavor Detectives
content.description: Think of your tongue as a team of flavor detectives! Different zones on the tongue specialize in finding sweet, salty, sour, and bitter tastes. But they can't work without their watery assistant, which dissolves the food first.

title: Step 4: Reveal - Taste Buds, Saliva, and Digestion
content: The tiny bumps on your tongue are called **Taste Buds**. The watery assistant in your mouth is **Saliva** (Lala-ras). Saliva doesn't just help you taste; it starts breaking down the food. This breaking down of food into simple forms your body can use is called **Digestion**. The food travels down the food pipe into the stomach, which acts like a mixer-grinder with digestive juices!

definition: Tiny sensory organs on the tongue that send flavor messages to the brain.
The watery liquid produced in the mouth that softens food and begins digestion.
The process of breaking down food into a simpler form so the body can get energy.

content: Remember the ancient Indian wisdom: 'Drink your solid food and chew your liquid food.' Chewing food 32 times ensures it mixes perfectly with saliva, making digestion easy!

question: Where does the digestion of food actually begin in our body?

content: Many students think the stomach is where digestion starts. But digestion actually begins right in your mouth when saliva mixes with your food!

title: Step 6: Reflection - The Glucose Mystery
content: When people are very sick or weak, they are often given a 'Glucose Drip' directly into their blood. Why don't they just eat food? Think about how long digestion takes and explain it in your own words.

title: Step 7: Connection - From Energy to Life
content: Tasting and digesting are just the first steps. The nutrients broken down in the stomach and intestines enter your blood and give you energy to play, think, and grow. Every system in your body relies on the fuel your digestive system creates!

title: Step 8: Mastery - The Digestion Journey Map
content: Draw a creative map of the 'Food Journey' starting from the Mouth, traveling down the Food Pipe, splashing into the Stomach's digestive juices, and finally moving to the Intestines. Label each part and write one sentence about its job!
